questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I was interested in universities with rich social environments and found that Yale-NUS College is a residential college which I was very excited about.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy. The website for Yale-NUS College is easily accessible and easy to navigate compared to many other universities.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I had a contact person who kept in touch and was beyond helpful. Because of Covid they could not pick me up at the airport but otherwise that is custom as well. I tested positive for Covid upon arrival and had to isolate for 10 days at my hotel, and Yale-NUS also assisted me through this process and even sent me care packages throughout my isolation.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Because of my covid isolation I did not participate in their orientation program, but they set up Zoom for the informational parts of orientation. However, even after orientation when I arrived after isolation everyone I met was beyond helpful and someone waited for me when I finally arrived on campus to introduce me and show me around.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Yale-NUS is a residential college meaning you have to live on campus. Therefore, housing is available for all students. You fill in a form before arrival answering your preferences for roommates (if you mind loud music, drinking alcohol etc) and they pair you with a suite from this form. You can also fill in whether you prefer living in a mixed suite, male suite or female suite and whether you prefer living in 4 person or 6 person suite.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: The rent you pay for living on campus includes meals at the dining hall which has many options for food. There are no kitchens in the suites, however some people buy microwave ovens or otherwise for their suite.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Living on campus is a wonderful experience and makes it very easy to become part of social life at college as an exchange students. I can only recommend.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Registration is very easy and you are guided through every step by Yale-NUS College. They will contact you anytime you need to fill out anything and help you through the process. Going on sem abroad can be overwhelming because of all the paper work, but for me it was very simple because of the help provided by Yale-NUS.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: As stated above I was guided by a contact from Yale-NUS through the process and I could also contact them if I had any questions or doubts.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was unsuccessful. Yale-NUS reserve spots in all classes for exchange students so you don't have to worry about classes filling up as much. However, exchange students sign up for classes only a few days before classes start which can be stressful and if you want to take classes in another field of study than from that which you study at home, you have to personally email the professor of the class and ask for permission to join. I thought this process of asking permission to join the class was automated and therefore, I didn't get the classes I wanted and only had time to sign up for anthropology classes. Overall the registration process is very different and much more complicated than at KU so be prepared for that.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Registration was confusing for me because it all had to be done very fast and I was still in isolation. I imagine that if I had been on campus I could have just popped by an office and instantly receive the help I needed so don't worry about it.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Classes are small so you get excellent tutoring from brilliant professors.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The workload is big as they have multiple assignments for each class and you have to be participating in class with questions and discussions. Thus, it can be difficult to skip readings and focus on assignments. However, the professors I had were very lenient towards exchange students and encouraged us to enjoy our time in Singapore and not stress.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The style of teaching is much more hands on. Studying anthropology I had to conduct several field researches on my own guided by my professors. It was an amazing experience since teaching back home has become much more distanced and about listening to lectures from professors. I have learned so much from my anthropology professors at Yale-NUS.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.answer:

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: My plane ended up being very expensive because of Covid fees. I also did not expect all the costs from just legal documents. Singapore's bureaucracy is very complicated and a lot of miscellaneous fees popped up from this.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Alcohol is also VERY expensive. However, if you eat food at hawker centers instead of restaurants, food is very cheap. Also the rent is excellent considering it INCLUDES meals from the dining hall. Basically if you're on a budget (as I was) you can survive your whole stay in Singapore on only the 4000,- each month. 
If you go you have to remember to either bring sheets and a cover for sleeping or buy something cheap at e.g., IKEA as the room you get only has the furniture and mattress and not the duvet or pillow or sheets. 
I have put 5,000 in "other fees" as Singapore is centrally placed in South East Asia and you definitely should travel a bit if you go.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were SO MANY clubs! Also they had an infinity pool, a swimming pool for athletic swimming, several dance studios, two fitness centers. They also had different clubs that can bring you around Singapore and so many activities throughout the semester. You will never be bored!

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: You should join their adventure club. I was a part of it and we went hiking, kayaking, and biking. At the end of sem they planned a hiking trip to the Malaysian Highlands.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: There are many places to go in Singapore and also islands around it which I mostly did since borders weren't open yet because of Covid. However, if borders had been open I would definitely have taken a bus to Malaysia and travelled around South East Asia on the weekends. Singapore is very small after all.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy for me at least. I did not feel any big differences from back home.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Just talk to them. They are open and curious to talk to other people and love to show exchange students around Singapore. I made friends for life there.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I did not find any challenging cultural differences on campus or with the Singaporean people, but I did find the amount of surveillance by the government challenging. Singapore is a very authoritarian state and I sometimes had a bit of anxiety by how controlling the government is and how much they keep and eye on everyone. Classes at Yale-NUS are not surveilled but classrooms at NUS which is right next by and where Yale-NUS sometimes borrow rooms are surveilled and even bugged.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Yale-NUS has 40% international students and I appreciated the diversity and the openness to talk about the world and each others cultures so so much.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Bring a sweater because the air condition is real.
Bring sunscreen because sunscreen in Singapore is expensive.
Don't eat pizza in Singapore - actually, don't eat any Italian or similar Western food because it is SO overpriced and it tastes crappy. Singaporean food tastes much, much better and is cheap at Hawker Centers.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Even though a lot of students take their studies very serious and can be found at the library 24 hours please don't let that freak you out. I was very chill with my studies and my professors was completely okay with that and I got good grades. So don't let the academic vibes scare you.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: All the friends I made. The students at YNC are so amazing, considerate, and inspiring.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: My whole experience with testing positive for Covid was very stressful because the health department lost my results and I had to go through the whole bureaucratic machine. But YNC was so helpful in the process.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
